findings.evidence_claim: subprocess.run(text=True) without encoding raises UnicodeDecodeError (ValueError) under non-UTF-8 locale for non-ASCII Go responses, escaping go_merge_config transport handling and crashing merge_config instead of one fallback warning.

go_merge_config resolves the gate binary via _orphans_bridge_home(None) (package parents[2]) and ignores materialize_recipes' ai_specs_home/cli_home, so under non-default homes the merge bridge misses the acquired binary and warns GO_MERGE_CONFIG_BRIDGE_FALLBACK per recipe per sync; bridge tests hide it via WORKTREE_GATE_BIN.

resolve_verified_binary accepts any executable with an existing .verified sidecar without digest re-check; a stale v0.24.0 cache binary fail-opens on the new --plan-merge-config flag (exit 0 empty stdout) causing one fallback warning per recipe per sync for projects without worktree-flow acquire.

pyRepr always single-quotes strings and escapes only backslash, apostrophe, \n, \r, \t; Python repr() switches to double quotes when the string contains an apostrophe and emits \xHH/\uXXXX for other controls, so enum-error messages diverge for containers holding such strings (both judges reported; B WARNING, A SUGGESTION).

For a declared empty array shape Go returns 'invalid shape declaration' while Python silently accepts empty and raises IndexError on non-empty; unreachable today because STRUCTURED_CONFIG_SHAPES only declares dict-topped shapes. INFO only, not in fix scope.
